1  high  A database listens beyond localhost and the host firewall does not restrict it (ubuntu)
   [db.listens_unfiltered]
   Subject       postgres (service 5432/tcp)
   You declared  engagement.yaml assets.ubuntu.context.expected_services[0]: Operator declaration at
                 assets.ubuntu.context.expected_services[0]
   Observed      net.listeners#1 (07:12, as deploy (sudo -n)): tcp 0.0.0.0:5432 (postgres); tcp
                 [::]:5432 (postgres)
   Observed      fw.ufw#1 (07:12, as deploy (sudo -n)): not installed (command not found)
   Observed      fw.firewalld#1 (07:12, as deploy): not installed (command not found)
   Observed      fw.nft#1 (07:12, as deploy): empty ruleset (no tables)
   Observed      fw.iptables_backend#1 (07:12, as deploy): /usr/sbin/xtables-nft-multi
   Concluded from declared:assets.ubuntu.context.expected_services[0], check:net.listeners,
                  check:fw.ufw, check:fw.firewalld, check:fw.nft, check:fw.iptables_backend
   Severity      high: base medium, +1 exposure internet (assets.ubuntu.context.exposure)
   Why here      You declared this host internet-facing, so this ranks one step higher. capped at
                 high: the cloud firewall and the service's own sign-in were not read, so scheck
                 cannot say anyone can use this now.
   Not checked   Whether a cloud firewall or security group blocks it was not assessed; who can sign
                 in to the database (pg_hba.conf, database users and passwords) was not read;
                 Filters outside nftables (eBPF programs such as Cilium's) were not read
   Fix           If only this host uses the database, bind it to localhost and restart it. If other
                 machines need it, allow the port only from their addresses. Check your cloud
                 firewall rules too: scheck did not read them.
                 Caveat: If ufw lets the port in by source port alone (from any port 53), delete
                   that rule (ufw status numbered, then ufw delete N): ufw already lets in replies
                   to the host's own DNS queries through connection tracking, so a source-port rule
                   is not needed.
                 Commands (review before running):
                   # only this host uses it: bind it to localhost, then restart the database
                   #   postgres: listen_addresses = 'localhost'
                   #   MySQL/MariaDB: bind-address = 127.0.0.1
                   #   Redis: bind 127.0.0.1
                   # other machines need it: allow only their addresses
                   sudo ufw default deny incoming
                   sudo ufw allow from 10.0.0.5 to any port 5432 proto tcp
